name: Granter
one_line: Chat-based agent, onboarded with the organisation's details and past applications, that matches funding calls, checks eligibility and admissibility, drafts applications section by section with playbooks, scores drafts with an Evaluator, and supports post-approval reporting. gamma_ray.fact_ray: 10 facts: 10 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.
gamma_ray.built_from: Granter's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)

configs.what: AI Grant Consultant with its documented defaults.

facts.label: The agent suggests; the person reviews and approves each action
facts.fact: The privacy policy, which covers the whole Granter platform and does not name the agent, says the platform's AI search, drafts, analyses and recommendations are suggestions that users review and approve before any submission or decision; it does not say each step is approved separately.
facts.quote: Users review and approve them before any submission or decision

facts.label: It retrieves information and recommends actions; a person acts
facts.fact: The product page says the agent finds calls, checks eligibility and runs an Evaluator that shows what to improve; the user selects the opportunity and makes the submission.
facts.quote: shows what to improve before you submit

facts.label: It works in one domain's data
facts.fact: The agent works in one domain: public and private funding calls at regional, national and EU level.
facts.quote: covers both public and private funding, at regional, national and EU level

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: The product page's FAQ says Granter does not submit the application: the user makes the final submission on the funding platform, since access to submission-platform accounts is restricted for Granter; this states who submits, a structural limit on the product, not an approval step.
facts.quote: The final submission is done by you on the relevant platform

facts.label: Its purpose and permitted tasks are stated in writing
facts.fact: The product page states the agent's purpose and tasks: find the calls an organisation qualifies for, check eligibility, draft the application against the call's criteria, review it, and manage reporting after approval; its FAQ says the agent does not submit.
facts.quote: It finds the calls you qualify for, drafts the application against the official criteria

facts.label: It tells the people it talks to that it is an AI
facts.fact: The privacy policy states that AI-generated content is labelled as such inside the platform; it is a label on generated content, not a statement about disclosure in conversation.
facts.quote: AI-generated content is presented as such inside the platform.

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: In a quote on the product page, Granter's CTO says onboarding collects the organisation's information, such as previous applications and institutional data, which the page says the agent then holds as context (vendor's statement).
facts.quote: collect all important information, like previous applications, institutional data

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Granter's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
